html:
The killing of striking dock workers at the Pidjiguiti quay in Bissau on 3 August 1959, when Portuguese police opened fire, killing about 50 people.

The workers wanted higher pay. After the shooting, Amilcar Cabral and the leaders of the PAIGC decided that peaceful protest in the towns could not work against the regime of Salazar. They moved to organising the peasants in the countryside, which led to the war of independence in 1963. The date, 3 August, is a national holiday.
sum: The killing of striking dock workers at the Pidjiguiti quay in Bissau on 3 August 1959, when Portuguese police opened fire, killing about 50 people.
